cards.problem: Teams needed to see how customers differed in needs, buying journeys and willingness to pay, rather than relying on an 'average' customer.

what_i_did.detail: Worked on interviews, surveys, in-home observation and pricing exercises so findings could be cross-checked.
Turned the findings into customer segment profiles and buying journeys.
Spelled out what each segment meant for product, message and sales channel, and was clear about the limits of the samples.

cards.artifacts: Surveys and interview guides, segment profiles, customer journeys, pricing analyses and client decks.
cards.outcome: Delivered segment profiles, journeys and pricing analyses for clients' model, pricing and marketing decisions.
cards.learning: Segmentation is a tool for making choices. The useful output is a clear picture of how customers behave and what that means for the product, message or channel.

cards.title: Choosing sales channels for a sunscreen launch in India
cards.headline: Researched consumers, competitors and distribution options for a Japanese personal-care company launching sunscreen in India, and built a channel strategy with potential partners.
cards.trigger: A Japanese personal-care company explored launching sunscreen in India.
cards.problem: The route to customers had to suit different customer groups, how they shop and the economics of each channel.

what_i_did.detail: Researched consumer groups and how each one shops for personal care.
Compared competitors and assessed distribution options and their economics.
Developed a channel strategy with potential distribution partners.

cards.artifacts: Consumer segments, a channel map, competitor analysis and market-entry recommendations.
cards.outcome: Delivered the channel strategy and market-entry recommendations.
cards.learning: Design channels around how customers actually buy, rather than assuming one route works nationwide.

cards.title: Repositioning a skincare brand in the US
cards.headline: Contributed market and competitor research to a Japanese skincare group's review of its US brand positioning, turning category and customer insight into positioning and product questions.
cards.trigger: A Japanese skincare group reviewed how its brand was positioned in the United States.
cards.problem: The work had to cover category trends, channels, competitors and why customers chose or rejected the brand.

what_i_did.detail: Contributed category, channel and trend research.
Mapped competitors and benchmarked products against the brand.
Helped turn the findings into positioning and product questions.

cards.artifacts: A category overview, competitor maps, a SWOT, product benchmarking and recommendations.
cards.outcome: Delivered the category review and positioning recommendations.
cards.learning: Test what makes a brand different against how customers talk and how competitors are sold.

cards.title: Pilot to improve customer experience at car dealerships
cards.headline: Helped design and run a plan-do-check-act pilot to improve customer experience across an automotive dealership network, turning advice into frontline roles, training, recognition and tool changes.
cards.trigger: An automotive dealership network wanted to improve how its staff engaged with customers.
cards.problem: Advice on better customer experience had to turn into what frontline staff actually did, how managers ran their teams, and tools that worked day to day.

what_i_did.detail: Translated customer-experience goals into specific changes to roles, processes and tools that could be tried in pilot dealerships.
Helped run the pilot in short cycles: try a change, check the results with staff and managers, adjust.

what_i_did.summary: Back it with training and recognition
what_i_did.detail: Designed training material and recognition so frontline staff had reasons and skills to adopt the changes.
Recorded lessons from each cycle to guide decisions on wider rollout.

cards.artifacts: Pilot plans, process maps, training material, review decks and action trackers.
cards.outcome: Delivered the pilot and a documented set of tested changes to guide the network's rollout decisions.
cards.learning: Frontline change needs clear owners and regular feedback. A strategy only becomes testable when it turns into daily actions reviewed with the people doing the work.

cards.title: Co-branding strategy to reach millennials for a legacy car brand
cards.headline: Screened partner brands for a legacy automotive brand trying to reach younger buyers, set the brand-fit criteria and built a roadmap for joint campaigns and how to measure them.
cards.trigger: A legacy automotive brand wanted to appeal to younger customers.
cards.problem: The right partner needed an overlapping audience and a good brand fit, followed by a practical plan for campaigns and measuring results.

what_i_did.detail: Helped set criteria for audience overlap and brand fit.
Assessed potential partner brands against those criteria.
Developed a roadmap for joint commercial and marketing work, with a way to evaluate results.

cards.artifacts: A partner shortlist, brand-fit analysis, a campaign roadmap and an evaluation approach.
cards.outcome: Delivered the partner shortlist and campaign roadmap.
cards.learning: Co-branding needs a believable link between the two audiences and a clear plan for what happens after the announcement.

cards.title: Reviewing the scope of my strategy role
cards.headline: Mapped my broad strategy and planning remit into workstreams six months in, which led to stock-takes of the market report and survey program that later cut vendor spend.
cards.trigger: My strategy and planning work had grown broad, and I needed a clear picture of what I was responsible for.
cards.problem: Explain a varied set of work without reducing it to a task list, and see where time was going versus where value was.

what_i_did.detail: Grouped my work into long-running workstreams and mapped the regular meetings and deliverables behind each.
Compared short-term requests with ongoing responsibilities to show where time was scattered.
Ran stock-takes of the monthly market report and the satisfaction survey, covering time spent, use and data quality.

cards.artifacts: Scope deck, work tracker, stock-takes of recurring reports.
cards.outcome: The review made expectations easier to discuss with my manager and set up the stock-takes that led to rebuilding the market report and rationalising research vendors.
cards.learning: Reviewing your scope from time to time is a practical tool, not just a look back. It separates reactive from strategic work and makes prioritising and handover easier.

cards.title: Comparing menu and in-store prices
cards.headline: Designed a repeatable method for comparing delivery menu prices with in-store prices across ANZ, with explicit matching rules and caveats.
cards.trigger: Strategy teams needed a consistent way to compare prices on delivery menus with prices in store.
cards.problem: Prices were collected through different channels, formats and times. The hard part was comparing them consistently.

what_i_did.detail: Set matching rules for which observations could be compared, with written exclusions and caveats.
Built a collection template and tracker for repeated data gathering.
Kept observed price differences separate from interpretation so people knew what the method could and couldn't show.

cards.artifacts: Measurement framework, collection template, tracker, research note.
cards.outcome: The team could discuss relative pricing without false precision, and the method fed the wider affordability measure.
cards.learning: Price comparisons are most credible when the matching rules, timing and handling of missing data are spelled out.

cards.title: Tracking restaurant selection and coverage
cards.headline: Built repeatable restaurant-selection reporting across ANZ with shared definitions and quality checks, so teams could tell real selection gaps from data problems.
cards.trigger: Teams needed a consistent view of which restaurants were on the platform and where the gaps were.
cards.problem: Teams used different definitions, data sources and reporting expectations, so gaps couldn't be compared fairly.

what_i_did.detail: Wrote clear metric definitions and the reporting logic behind each view.
Added routine quality checks and transparent handling of exceptions.
Organised outputs so market teams could tell data problems apart from real selection gaps.

cards.artifacts: Workbooks, dashboard views, metric definitions, comparison checks.
cards.outcome: Coverage reviews became repeatable, and selection measures fed the regional growth program's tracker.
cards.learning: Selection reporting is more actionable when keeping definitions consistent is treated as part of the job.

cards.title: Field research on how drivers use connected-car services
cards.headline: Helped design and run ethnographic field research into how Indian drivers use their vehicles and digital services, turning observation and interviews into concrete service-design questions for a car maker.
cards.trigger: A car maker wanted new connected-car features grounded in how drivers actually live with their vehicles.
cards.problem: Feature ideas needed to rest on drivers' real motivations, habits and frustrations, which usual product assumptions could miss. The sample was small, so findings had to be framed carefully.

what_i_did.detail: Helped design research that combined observing drivers in daily use with in-depth interviews.
Grouped findings around behaviours, attitudes and unmet needs rather than by feature.
Turned what we heard into service-design questions to test, while being clear about the limits of a small sample.

cards.artifacts: Interview guides, fieldwork summaries, customer journey maps and insight decks.
cards.outcome: Delivered journey maps and insight decks that reframed the questions the product team was asking about connected services.
cards.learning: This kind of research is most useful when it changes the questions a product team asks. It should spark ideas to test, not stand in for the whole market.

cards.title: Mapping research partnerships between India and Japan
cards.headline: Contributed to a public-sector study mapping opportunities for joint research and startup support between India and Japan, organising desk research and interviews into a comparable map of institutions and barriers.
cards.trigger: A public-sector study needed to identify where India and Japan could collaborate on research and startup support.
cards.problem: The study needed a comparable picture of institutions, how they already worked together and what got in the way. A simple directory of organisations wouldn't do.

what_i_did.detail: Helped organise desk research into a map of potential partner institutions and existing collaboration.
Used expert interviews to find practical barriers that documents didn't show.
Kept documented activity apart from opportunities that would need to be checked directly.

cards.artifacts: An institution map, interview notes, research reports and an executive summary.
cards.outcome: Delivered the institution map and executive summary for the client's partnership discussions.
cards.learning: These studies are most useful when they link the landscape to specific partnership questions and show where the evidence is thin.

cards.title: Benchmarking battery suppliers
cards.headline: Benchmarked battery suppliers for an industrial client on capacity, terms, delivery record and fit, and helped draft a sourcing plan with criteria for choosing and negotiating with vendors.
cards.trigger: An industrial client was considering a more coordinated way to buy batteries.
cards.problem: Choosing suppliers meant weighing supply capacity, terms, delivery record and strategic fit.

what_i_did.detail: Assessed supplier and competitor information on capacity, terms and delivery record.
Laid out the trade-offs and assumptions behind each sourcing option.
Helped draft criteria for choosing and negotiating with vendors.

cards.artifacts: A supplier assessment, a benchmark, sourcing options and proposal material.
cards.outcome: Delivered the supplier benchmark and sourcing options.
cards.learning: A sourcing recommendation is stronger when it shows the trade-offs and assumptions behind the shortlist.

cards.title: Sales and service playbook for a luxury car brand
cards.headline: Researched what luxury car buyers expect and helped write step-by-step sales procedures covering the full journey from first enquiry to after-sales.
cards.trigger: A luxury automotive brand wanted every customer to get the same experience.
cards.problem: The process had to cover everything from the first enquiry to after the sale, while meeting premium service expectations.

what_i_did.detail: Researched what luxury customers expected at each stage of buying and owning.
Mapped the end-to-end customer journey and the moments that mattered most.
Helped write sales procedures with steps that could be observed and coached, plus rollout guidance.

cards.artifacts: A customer study, a journey map, sales procedures and rollout guidance.
cards.outcome: Delivered the sales playbook and rollout guidance for the brand's network.
cards.learning: A service standard works when its steps can be observed and frontline staff back it.

cards.title: Business development: proposals and client account management
cards.headline: Wrote client proposals and sales material, coordinated client accounts across India and Japan, and set up an organised way to reuse past work so proposals stayed tailored without starting from scratch.
cards.trigger: Alongside project work, the consulting team needed to win new work and keep client relationships strong.
cards.problem: Proposals had to be tailored and on time, and past work had to be easy to reuse without making every pitch generic.

what_i_did.detail: Wrote proposals, credentials and sales material tailored to each client's question.
Coordinated client accounts and briefs between project work.
Set up a knowledge library and trackers so past delivery evidence could be reused quickly in new proposals.

cards.artifacts: Proposals, credentials, client briefs, a knowledge library and trackers.
cards.outcome: Built a reusable library of past work that made tailored proposals faster to put together.
cards.learning: Winning work is easier when evidence of past delivery is easy to find and each proposal stays specific to the client.
